title: Introduce interleaved cohort resilience simulator and memory snapshot tee
author: Elliot Chen
description: Adds a new benchmark harness that simulates interleaved priming/cohort access patterns to exercise KV-cache reuse and memory churn across GPUs, paired with a lightweight snapshot "tee" that captures per-epoch memory liveness metadata to an external object store for offline analysis. Motivation: we observed production tail regressions correlated with nonuniform priming across tenant cohorts; existing runners either target pure single-stream warmup or broad-stroke mixed loads but don't capture liveness metadata needed to diagnose persistent allocation hotspots. This PR introduces an extensible simulator, a memory-snapshot tee, new microbenchmarks and a reporting pipeline that produces compact epochal liveness histograms and object-store artifacts for flamegraph correlation. The description below lists commits, changed areas, CI summary, review thread highlights and perf baseline, and notes about rollout and follow-ups.

ci_checks_log: unit-tests: passed (fast smoke), full scenario run: passed on second attempt
benchmark-pipeline: uploaded artifacts to ephemeral bucket (succeeded)
perf_results_summary: Baseline microbench (kv_reuse_microbench) shows a 18% regression in reuse ratio for heavily interleaved cohorts versus single-stream warmup on our reference A100 profile; end-to-end scenario p95 latency increased by ~6% under worst-case skew but average token cost remained within 3%. Memory liveness snapshots revealed a small persistent slab retained across epochs caused by prefetch threads; we added a mitigation note and a follow-up ticket to instrument allocator lifetimes.
release_notes: - New interleaved cohort simulator for workload fidelity testing. - Memory snapshot tee exports per-epoch liveness histograms for offline analysis. - Added microbench for KV cache reuse measurement.
merge_outcome: merged after 2 approvals and CI green; squash-merged to main
post_merge_actions: Deployed bench-pipeline change to canary CI, created ENG-4217 to track follow-up allocator instrumentation and ENG-4220 for production monitoring dashboards
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative about adding runtime hooks; the snapshot tee runs outside the hot path and is opt-in via config. The provided analysis notebook in docs/benchmarks shows how to join snapshot artifacts with flamegraphs to find candidate allocation lifetimes.
